scope: Finite 40-bit mixed-pair cycle certificate. The 22 split primes through 177 lie in the order-198850 cycle generated by 5. An exhaustive scan through 100000 finds ten gap targets with order above the window and index above D^(1/4); all have exponent-1/2/3 pair hits. Determinants are multiples of the cycle order, and the two-part extractor returns 1000003. A full-rank base plus one hit per target gives rank 32 and determinant 96768h; the pair rows alone give a rank-32 edge basis at window 2 with selected minor 8192h and row-lattice index 16h; at window 3 their row-lattice index is h, the full relation kernel; four exponent-3 base-gap rows saturate the window-2 index 16h to h. A pure-order diagonal control also extracts the factor, using the enumerated cycle and its orders; it is not a factoring algorithm. An isolated-column repair control on all split primes through 500 fills the one zero pair-row column (229) with a common-annihilator row. No uniform pair-basis, rank-window, first-hit, or smoothness theorem is claimed.
